transcript: [00:00] Liam Chen: hey everybody thanks for hopping on, I think we have about 50 minutes, uh so we're going to focus on Optimize and the quantization profiles — INT8 and FP8 — and then a quick quality vs latency walkthrough. Sofia will drive the demo.

[02:05] Sofia Patel: cool thanks liam, hi maya, ethan, sara — quick agenda: how Optimize recommends profiles, what the console looks like, sample benchmark results, and then a live example of switching profiles and what that does to latency and output.

[04:12] Maya Lopez: sounds good. high level, our constraints: we need 95th pct latency < 250ms for chat path, 99th around 350ms, and 80% cost reduction target vs current on-prem setup. also concerned about any quality regressions in ecomm intent classification.
[06:20] Ethan Park: yea and our payloads are variable — short prompts like product lookup and longer session context for recommendations. we care about KV cache behaviors too.

[08:03] Sofia Patel: okay great context. quick note: Optimize has precomputed quant profiles per model family — we profile across sequence lengths and pick int8, fp8 candidates. We also surface an expected quality delta (measured by your eval set) and latency percentiles.

[10:30] Liam Chen: and to be clear, when we say FP8 we mean the mixed 8-bit floating variant — sometimes the transcript says F P 8, sorry the auto-transcript messes that up — but it's the same thing our runtime supports.

[12:15] Sofia Patel: jumping into the console — here you can see a model (redwood-rlm-1-like), the Optimize tab shows recommended profiles: "balanced-int8", "latency-fp8", and "high-precision-fp16". each profile has estimated throughput, token cost, and a quality delta.

[15:00] Sofia Patel: (shares screen) here's the latency chart: orange is balanced-int8, blue is latency-fp8. we ran internal bench on A100-like hardware with 2048 warmup tokens and 256 sequence length distribution similar to your traces. INT8 gave ~2.8x throughput vs fp16 and lower cost, but the quality delta on our rouge-like evaluation was about -1.8% for some gen tasks.
[18:20] Ethan Park: that -1.8% on rouge, is that on your generic eval or a redwood-curated ecomm intent set? how would that translate to our classification thresholds?

[19:10] Sofia Patel: good question — that was on our internal news-gen set. we recommend running a small eval with your prompt set; Optimize can ingest your evals and show per-prompt quality deltas. for intents it's often smaller — we've seen 0.2-0.7% in many ecomm intent sets when well-calibrated.
[22:00] Maya Lopez: ok but we need to be conservative; if we see regression we want automatic fallback. does Redwood support runtime fallback to a higher-precision variant?

[23:05] Liam Chen: yes — routing policies and automatic fallback exist. you can set per-route SLOs, and when latency or quality metrics break thresholds we can route to a non-quantized or FP16 variant. that's part of the rollout policy in the console.

[26:40] Sofia Patel: walking through a live test — I change the profile from high-precision to balanced-int8 for this route. you'll see the 95th and 99th latency drop immediately in the live trace panel; the sampling 1K requests we ran showed 95th go from 420ms to 160ms.
[29:50] Sara McCoy: whoa 160ms at 95th is great. what's the hardware assumption? and does that include network egress in our VPC case?

[31:05] Sofia Patel: benchmark is server-side only on a p4-like machine. for VPC/private deployments we can share end-to-end test harness. network overhead depends on your infra; typical VPC add 10-30ms depending on region and peering.
[33:20] Ethan Park: what about batching? some of our endpoints are high qps. does int8 change batching behavior?

[34:15] Sofia Patel: int8 allows larger batch sizes due to reduced memory, so you can increase batching and improve throughput while preserving latency SLOs with smart batching policies in the runtime. batching policy can be workload-aware.

[36:40] Liam Chen: another practical point — when you quantize aggressively you may break some edge-case deterministic behaviors. we recommend a canary first, run eval sets, then expand. Optimize gives you a per-prompt delta heatmap to find risky prompts.
[39:00] Sofia Patel: demoing the per-prompt heatmap now — see this cluster of prompts where INT8 drops score. you can flag those prompts and have those hit FP16. it's per-route split configs.
[41:50] Maya Lopez: security wise we need to know about key management and audit logs if we do private deployment and POC. are profile changes audited?

[43:00] Liam Chen: yes, console writes all rollout and profile changes to audit logs and we integrate with KMS for key management. Private customers can bring their own KMS/HSM. we'll send SOC2 and our security pack as a follow up.

[45:20] Ethan Park: okay timeline — we'd like to run a POC with our 10K prompt set, measure 95/99 latencies and accuracy tradeoffs. we'd also like a cost projection for dedicated capacity for our expected QPS.

[47:10] Sofia Patel: next steps: we'll run a baseline harness with your traces, push INT8 and FP8 runs, and produce a report. I'll include expected token cost and estimated savings vs your current infra.
[50:05] Maya Lopez: perfect. one last nit — do you have any guidance on models that don't quantize well? we've seen some Llama-derivative variants be finicky.
[51:30] Sofia Patel: yes some model families respond worse to 8-bit quantization; Optimize flags those and recommends FP8 or hybrid-quant. we'll test your specific model variant in the POC.
[51:55] Liam Chen: great thanks everyone, we'll follow up with the spreadsheet and runbook. meeting adjourned.
